reason: The report's 2.17 estimate comes from a single unadjusted regression. Adding the pre-period controls (firm size, prior productivity and others) cuts the training coefficient to about 0.5–0.6, with p of roughly 0.01–0.02. Firm size alone cuts it to 1.18, so the headline effect is largely confounding. The report also tested only one specification and used an arbitrary 1% trim, so a size of 2.2 is not supported.
